minutes.headline: Commissioners leaned toward a health-insurance buyback near five thousand dollars and urged speed on PFAS treatment funding.
minutes.summary: The commission approved the prior minutes, then went through revised personnel policies and benefits: Juneteenth and floating holidays, part-time vacation, and an insurance buyback modelled on other towns. It then discussed the new EPA PFAS advisories, the Hickory Hills well pilot study, a possible special meeting, and adding water main work to a state revolving fund application. Only the minutes were voted; the policy changes and special meeting were set for the next agenda.

what_happened.line: Commissioners moved to add Juneteenth to the paid holiday list and to cover part-time employees in the vacation wording, prorated to normal hours.
Staff were asked to draft an insurance buyback policy, with a proof-of-coverage form, for the next meeting; five thousand was the working amount.
The commission discussed the new EPA PFAS advisories and the Hickory Hills pilot study; a special meeting is to go on the next agenda, with Hickory Hills invited.
Water main replacement is to be added to the state revolving fund application, which is due in August.
Only the prior minutes were voted on; the personnel policy changes were set for the next agenda and no other votes were taken.

why_it_matters: A buyback for declining district health insurance, and the new holiday and part-time leave wording, change what the district pays for staff benefits, and so what water rates have to cover.
If PFAS treatment is mandated without grant help, a member estimated rates could rise several-fold, so the state revolving fund application and the pilot study bear on future water bills.
